idle_trace.scope: machine_suspend begin through first subsequent device PM callback

battery.measurement_scope: Entire capture, including awake and suspend/resume overhead
battery.power_check_scope: Endpoints only; keep all external power disconnected throughout

assessment: Fourth healthy captured suspend after reboot, including a long backpack sleep and two apps-open tabletop runs. No recurrence of the earlier half-second idle-exit loop.
counter_note: Kernel totals include one additional successful suspend outside the four captured post-reboot tests.
learning: The same patched kernel and enabled flag support both the earlier bad state and subsequent healthy long and repeated sleeps; a newly changed kernel binary is not the established cause.
Simply opening the user-reported apps, including Slack, did not reproduce the previous high-power idle pattern in two captured runs.
A single suspend/resume cycle does not invariably cause the bad state; recovery persisted through repeated cycles.
The trigger that creates the previous high-power state remains unidentified. Reboot coincided with driver/hardware reinitialization and a fresh app/session state.
limitations: Whole-capture power is 2.8351 W, including 67.95 seconds outside suspend, rather than isolated steady-state power.
These tests do not establish indefinite or overnight reliability or exclude a specific app workload or device transition as a trigger.
next_step: Retain the working kernel and flag; use normal workload and preserve a capture before reboot if heat or drain returns, to identify the transition into the bad state.
